Its after-reads of other actors' state are keyed to the round right after `XS-2`: `gate.py run --live-legs` fires them in its span, in block order, and the wrap's light gate never re-fires them (`inputs#I3` item 3). Then come the census keyed `operator` and the leg-less after-reads of `XS-2`'s own products, all after the span; then after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers); then the operator pass. **Revision 1:** entries 1–8 (phase A) are not re-fired; implement starts at entry 9 (step 18). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` and `XS-2` are ledgered in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is the running total of base lines in that one file (`XS` stands as line 1, so `XS-2` is `--cap 2`). The census after the last live leg is keyed `operator` and stands after the span.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each fires on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases (ids within 16 characters, `inputs#I3` items 1–2). It reads «holds» only when its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Its after-reads of other actors' state are keyed to the round right after `XS-2`: `gate.py run --live-legs` fires them in its span, in block order, and the wrap's light gate never re-fires them (`inputs#I3` item 3). Then come the census keyed `operator` and the leg-less after-reads of `XS-2`'s own products, all after the span; then after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers); then the operator pass. **Revision 1:** entries 1–8 (phase A) are not re-fired; implement starts at entry 9 (step 18). What is not run, and why: no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); between phase B and the landing no stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` and `XS-2` are ledgered in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is the running total of base lines in that one file (`XS` stands as line 1, so `XS-2` is `--cap 2`). The census after the last live leg is keyed `operator` and stands after the span.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each fires on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases (ids within 16 characters, `inputs#I3` items 1–2). It reads «holds» only when its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Each filter selects 0 tests on the tree before its case exists and at least one once it does. Revision 1 re-fires the three standing controls and adds `address-shape`:

prose.text: The block runs in this order: phase A (formatter, linter, the agent crate's and the root bin's unit cases, the canary binary, then the workspace unit, integration and E2E layers on 28 rows); phase B (formatter, linter, the agent crate, the rig's library cases, the root bin, the row's `cli_verify` cases, the canary binary), then the four filtered control entries; the round (entries 20–34, `round` and `live` entries ONLY, `inputs#I8` item 8). Its after-reads of other actors' state are keyed to the round right after `XS-2`: `gate.py run --live-legs` fires them in its span, in block order, and the wrap's light gate never re-fires them (`inputs#I3` item 3). Then come the census keyed `operator` and the leg-less after-reads of `XS-2`'s own products, all after the span; then after the landing (`diff -r`, the three layers); then the operator pass. **Revision 1:** entries 1–8 (phase A) are not re-fired; implement starts at entry 9 (step 18). What is not run, and why: no mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10); no release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it); between phase B and the landing no stamped-home suite runs (§Steps intro). Every test start runs under a test-owned home and user home; every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint. The live start runs under the rig's private scratch; the rig's `--deadline` bounds it under the entry's `timeout`. The live leg's non-priming probes are the round entries ahead of it. `XS` and `XS-2` are ledgered in `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-cross-session-prefix-ledger-row/evidence/cross-starts.ndjson`; `--cap` is the running total of base lines in that one file (`XS` stands as line 1, so `XS-2` is `--cap 2`). The census after the last live leg is keyed `operator` and stands after the span.

**The remove-the-guard controls** are implement's one-shot `gate.py control` runs, never entries. Each fires on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases (ids within 16 characters, `inputs#I3` items 1–2). It reads «holds» only when its own case ran and FAILED with no TIMEOUT line. Each filter selects 0 tests on the tree before its case exists and at least one once it does. Revision 1 re-fires the three standing controls and adds `address-shape`:
